A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RFWave work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original listening tests, objective reconstruction measurements, ablations, and inference-speed benchmarks in Tables 1–4 and A.5–A.6.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds GAN comparisons, cross-domain evaluation, sampling and backbone analyses, and resource measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds equal-straightness selection of nonuniform Euler sampling times, with implementation in Appendix A.5. This refines inference while retaining the multi-band architecture, ConvNeXtV2 backbone, normalization procedures, and three training losses. Appendix A.4 documents existing STFT losses rather than introducing another objective.

E1.justification: The existing training corpora and broad speech, singing, music, and codec coverage remain. v3 adds a focused scenario: Mel-spectrogram reconstruction on MUSDB18 using LibriTTS-trained models, covering vocals, drums, bass, other instruments, and mixtures. MUSDB18 already contributed codec-test samples in v2; its speech-to-music transfer role is new.

E2.justification: BigVGAN becomes an evaluated comparator in quality and speed benchmarks, and Table 6 adds DDPM and ResNet alternatives. Vocos is removed from the original multi-dataset comparison in Tables 1 and A.5 and its corresponding spectrogram panels, while participating in separate GAN comparisons. The Vocos, PriorGrad, and FreGrad rows from v2's LJSpeech ablation table also disappear.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a separate GAN listening study, a 50-step DDPM control, a similarly sized ResNet backbone, and half/double-size model configurations. The speed benchmark adds GPU-memory measurement and explicit 44.1-kHz comparisons. These extend the experimental protocol substantially; the retained default training configuration and ten-step RFWave budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of equal-straightness sampling, Rectified Flow versus DDPM, backbone choice, model scaling, and speech-to-music generalization. Figures A.8–A.9 newly illustrate artifacts from omitting STFT and overlap losses. Conversely, the frequency-domain energy-balanced variant and two CFG ablation rows reported in v2 are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report MOS with confidence intervals, explicitly identified as 95% intervals in Table 1. Additional interval-bearing results in v3 use the existing reporting practice. Neither version supplies training-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results: MUSDB18 average MOS is 3.67 for RFWave, 3.51 for BigVGAN, and 3.10 for Vocos; the equal-straightness ablation reports PESQ 4.275 versus 4.211 without it. Reported RFWave speed changes from 97.01 to 162.59 times real-time, without explaining the cause. Original diffusion and EnCodec scores are largely retained, while some Vocos/CFG entries disappear. The new LibriTTS MOS comparison is explicitly a separate listening study.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 introduces the straightness functional S(v) and uses equal accumulated deviation to define sampling intervals. The original Rectified Flow and loss equations remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added. Appendix A.4 mainly supplies formulas for previously specified STFT-loss components.

C1.justification: The central claims about efficient, high-quality, frame-level multi-band reconstruction remain. v3 adds sampling-time selection as a fourth stated contribution, updates the headline speed from 97 to 160 times real-time, and explicitly claims speed comparable to GAN-based methods in the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations connecting time-domain performance to periodic signals introduced by ISTFT, relating this mechanism to Snake activation, and attributing cross-domain advantages to better preserved harmonics. It also discusses the necessity of Rectified Flow, backbone efficiency, and scaling tradeoffs. Earlier discussion of MBD's sound-effect strengths and CFG's approximately 50% latency overhead is removed.

D1.justification: New details include sampling-grid calibration using one batch of 96 examples and 100 integration steps, half/double-size backbone configurations, explicit STFT-loss formulas, and the BigVGAN repository. Most optimizer, preprocessing, hardware, and training-duration information is retained. v3 omits v2's explicit Mel-test subset sizes of 20, 300, and 50; this establishes reduced documentation, not changed sample selection.

R1.justification: v3 expands context through references to flow matching, stochastic interpolants, additional diffusion vocoders, and BigVGAN/Snake, and explicitly distinguishes energy-balanced loss from PriorGrad's adaptive prior. Some codec and future-TTS references are removed. These refine the existing research positioning; citation-style and bibliography-format changes do not themselves constitute substantive changes.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively condensed and rewritten. Previously separate experiment and results sections become a structured experiments-and-analysis section separating diffusion, GAN, codec, ablation, and speed evaluations. Subband details move to the appendix, appendix explanations are reorganized, and the conclusion loses the future-TTS and ethical-concerns discussion.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn as an integrated architecture diagram. Existing spectrogram comparisons change from five to four panels, while new sampling, GAN-comparison, and loss-effect figures are added. Tables are reorganized around separate comparison groups, and the speed table gains memory and high-sample-rate entries. The document also adopts different headers, typography, and table formatting.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation through speech-to-music transfer tests, BigVGAN comparisons, controls isolating Rectified Flow and backbone choices, and diagnostic loss examples (Tables 2–6; Figures A.6–A.9). These address important gaps in evidence for generalization and design decisions in v2. Some earlier Vocos/CFG results and explicit test-subset counts are lost, and the speed revision is unexplained, but the added diagnostic and comparative evidence provides a substantial net quality gain.
